tasks.old_behavior: During Ruby process exit (rb_ec_teardown), if rb_vm_trap_exit() raises an exception (TAG != NONE), the trap error was silently discarded. ec->errinfo was not preserved. After EC_POP_TAG, rb_ec_exec_end_proc would run, potentially overwriting errinfo with END handler errors. EXIT trap exceptions could be lost entirely.
tasks.new_behavior: During Ruby process exit, if rb_vm_trap_exit() raises an exception, the trap error is saved in a local trap_errinfo variable. ec->errinfo is cleared to Qnil before END procs run. After END procs complete, the trap error is reported via error_handle() and ec->errinfo is restored to trap_errinfo. This ensures EXIT handler exceptions are preserved and reported after END block handlers, without loss.
tasks.compatibility_reason: The side effect of error reporting during Ruby process exit cleanup changes observably. Any Ruby program that registers both Signal.trap(:EXIT) and END/at_exit blocks which raise exceptions will produce different error output after this patch. Previously, EXIT handler exceptions could be silently lost; now they are always reported. END handler error output may also differ because shown_causes are shared via add_shown_cause() in eval_jump.c to prevent duplicate cause chains. This affects the externally visible diagnostic output during crash/exit reporting.
tasks.test_recommendation: Create Ruby scripts with combinations of Signal.trap(:EXIT) raising exceptions and multiple END blocks raising exceptions. Compare before/after stderr output for correctness and completeness.

tasks.old_behavior: When multiple END/at_exit handlers raised exceptions, each handler's error was independently reported via error_handle() without tracking already-shown causes. This could cause duplicate cause chain output in error messages. EXIT handler errors were processed by rb_ec_teardown before END handlers, potentially being lost when END handlers also failed.
tasks.new_behavior: END handler errors now share a common shown_causes accumulator (add_shown_cause in eval_jump.c). When an END handler raises, its errinfo is recorded as a shown cause before the next handler runs, preventing duplicate cause reporting. EXIT handler errors are now processed AFTER END handlers in rb_ec_teardown, ensuring they are visible. The error_handle_with_shown_causes function in eval_error.c accepts an external shown_causes pointer to enable this sharing.
tasks.compatibility_reason: Exception reporting during Ruby process cleanup changes observably. Programs with multiple END blocks that chain exceptions AND an EXIT trap will see different error messages: duplicate causes are eliminated, and EXIT trap exceptions now appear in output. Test suites that assert on specific exception messages or counts during exit will be affected. The error_handle function is now a thin wrapper around error_handle_with_shown_causes, preserving the public API signature but changing internal error routing.
